text:
Samira Patel: Heads-up — provisioning for several private GPU clusters in ap-southeast started failing ~10m ago. Seen a bunch of KMS Deny errors in the bootstrap logs.

Liam O'Connor: On it. Which job? any recent infra changes?

Samira Patel: The EC2 autoscaler job that tags subnets for private-provisioning rolled a change yesterday (infra PR #4127). It updated subnet tag key from "redwood:env" to "env:role".

oncall-sre: @Samira can you paste the error dump?

Samira Patel: Sure — excerpt from bootstrap: 
```
2026-03-18T22:04:12Z ERROR failed to create kms key alias: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/provisioner is not authorized to perform: kms:CreateAlias on resource: arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:444455556666:key/abcd-1234
status code: 400, request id: 5f3d...
```

Samira Patel: Security bot also fired an audit alert for cross-account KMS policy mismatch.

security-bot: [alert] KMS policy denies CreateAlias for role:provisioner — policy contains conditional on subnet tag redwood:env == private.

Rajesh Iyer: That matches. We have a conditional KMS policy that allows provisioning only when the subnet carries tag redwood:env=private. Changing tag key breaks the condition -> deny.

Liam O'Connor: Ugh. That explains the immediate KMS denies. Why did PR change the tag key?

Samira Patel: PR aimed to standardize keys across stacks. Missed the downstream IAM/KMS conditions.

Rajesh Iyer: Quick remediation options: 1) revert the tag-key change on the affected subnets, 2) update KMS policy to accept the new tag key (needs security review), or 3) add a temporary policy exception for the provisioner role. Revert is fastest.

oncall-sre: Revert sounds safest to unstick capacity. Is there a chance other regions are affected?

Samira Patel: We only flipped keys in ap-southeast and eu-west during the rollout. eu-west hasn't hit provisioning yet but same risk.

Liam O'Connor: Cost note: when provisioning failed some fleets fell back to hosted GPU pool which spiked spend on spot instances. Finance flagged a ~$5k anomaly this morning. We should avoid bouncing customers to hosted until fixed.

Rajesh Iyer: I'll patch the provisioner role and KMS policy in parallel but will not push policy changes without sec sign-off. Rolling revert of tags now.

deploy-bot: Started run: infra/revert-subnet-tag-change (PR 4155) — applying to ap-southeast-1 subnets (4 of 4).

Samira Patel: Confirming command I ran: 
```bash
aws ec2 create-tags --resources subnet-0a1b2c3d --tags Key=redwood:env,Value=private --region ap-southeast-1
```

oncall-sre: After revert, run a small provisioning sanity check (1 GPU) and tail bootstrap logs for KMS errors.

Samira Patel: Sanity check passed — provisioning succeeded for cluster test-provision-01. No KMS denies in logs.

security-bot: [info] Audit event: tag-change revert by Samira Patel; triggered replay of related KMS denies for investigation.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks. Can we add an automated test in the infra pipeline to flag tag-dependent IAM/KMS conditions? This slipped through manual review.

Rajesh Iyer: Agreed — will open a follow-up: infra-ops#789 (add tag-condition test + docs). Also will queue a security review to consider relaxing the KMS policy conditions so they are resilient to key rename.

Samira Patel: Note for postmortem: include cost impact (~$5k) and a checklist: 1) tag-change rollout plan, 2) KMS/IAM dependency mapping, 3) canary provisioning after tag changes.

oncall-sre: Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep open until eu-west rollout is verified.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks team.

Rajesh Iyer: I'll follow up with sec for policy patch.

Samira Patel: Closing thread once eu-west is confirmed.

(emoji reactions: :white_check_mark: :lock: :money_with_wings:)
